tools.name: submit_event
tools.description: Send an in-person event in the Greater Toronto Area to Lalawe's review queue. Requirements, all checked: the event happens in person in the GTA (Toronto, Peel, York, Durham or Halton region); it hasn't ended (Toronto time); the title and description are given in BOTH English (title, description) and

tools.name: check_submission
tools.description: Look up the review status of a submission by the id submit_event returned: pending, approved (with the event's public URL) or rejected (with the reviewer's reason).

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "submit_event" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Send an in-person event in the Greater Toronto Area to Lalawe's review queue. Requirements, all checked: the event happens in person in the GTA (Toronto, Peel, …

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: submit_event, check_submission · Public sink: submit_event.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: submit_event, check_submission · Public sink: submit_event

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
